title: Route nightly reprocessing to the Batches API, keep the upload flow synchronous
correct_option_text: Route the nightly archive reprocessing through the Message Batches API and keep interactive validation on synchronous Messages API calls.
why: Batches cost 50% of standard prices but may take up to 24 hours and carry no latency guarantee. Latency-tolerant work (nightly archive, audits, next-day reports) goes to batch; a user waiting to correct and submit a document stays on synchronous calls. 'Most batches finish within an hour' is not a service level.
rubric: Learner justifies each route by who is waiting and by when the result is needed.
Learner states the two batch trade-offs (price, processing window) without quoting the 1-hour figure as a guarantee.
Learner explains why the SLA for a nightly job still needs a submission cut-off time.
task: Run the two workloads from the case file through the routing rule: the interactive upload (one document, user waiting) goes through the synchronous path and is timed; the nightly archive (all documents, reviewed next day) goes through the Message Batches API. Record the routing table and the cost ratio.
prompt_template: Workload: {{workload_name}} · blocking: {{blocking}} · deadline: {{deadline}} · documents: {{document_count}} -> route to {{route}}

routing.decision_line: Workload: interactive_upload · blocking: True · deadline: user is waiting (seconds) · documents: 1 -> route to sync Messages API
Workload: nightly_archive · blocking: False · deadline: next business day 09:00 · documents: 7 -> route to Message Batches API

result.note: results reviewed next day; up to 24 h processing window, no latency guarantee

rule: blocking user flow -> synchronous; latency-tolerant volume -> batch at 50% price
